trust_decision.summary: Whether a response carrying Set-Cookie may be stored in, kept in, or re-served from a cache operating as type 'shared'; decided in canCacheResponse / revalidationResponseDisallowsCachedReuse (cache-handler.js) and in the interceptor's handleResult / revalidation callback (interceptor/cache.js).

landing_point.why: canCacheResponse already holds the analogous shared-cache rule (shared && private => do not store); an engineer reading 'Set-Cookie caching in shared caches' adds the header test here.

fix_sites.entry_point: interceptors.cache() -> CacheHandler.onResponseStart (304 revalidation with no cache-control/expires reaches early return; fix hoists revalidationResponseDisallowsCachedReuse above it, fix.diff:12-18)
interceptors.cache() -> CacheHandler.onResponseStart 304 branch, incl. stale-while-revalidate background revalidation (lib/interceptor/cache.js:415)
interceptors.cache() -> handleResult reading an existing entry from the store (MemoryCacheStore/SqliteCacheStore shared with a private-type interceptor or written by an older undici)
fix_sites.module_kind: interceptor (read-time guard over persisted store state)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/interceptor/cache.js:375-379 (read-time rejection of stored entries; fix.diff:75-84); state produced by lib/cache/sqlite-cache-store.js:233-253 / lib/cache/memory-cache-store.js:93-108

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once the write path refuses Set-Cookie for shared caches nothing new can land in the store, so filtering on read looks redundant; a store shared between a private and a shared interceptor, or a persisted SQLite file from an older version, reads as an unsupported configuration.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A cache of type 'private' must keep storing and re-serving Set-Cookie responses (fix test fix.diff:142-202 serves user-a's cookie from cache via privateClient); qualified private="h"/no-cache="h" and Connection-listed header stripping must keep caching the rest of the shared response. Applying the check regardless of type, or refusing on any header-stripping directive, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: set-cookie as array (presence test via Object.hasOwn, fix.diff:38,50)
set-cookie with empty value (presence, not truthiness)
304 revalidation response with no cache-control/expires (early-return route, fix.diff:12-18)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: 304 merge path copies cachedValue.headers into a new entry; a sibling could add a merge helper that re-attaches set-cookie from the stored entry after the storability check ran on the 304's own headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The merge already happens after canCacheResponse inspected only the 304 headers; a maintainer refactoring header merging would not re-run the check on the merged result (how-type: rename/merge after check).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: read-time guard keyed on exact lowercase 'set-cookie' while a custom CacheStore returns mixed-case header keys
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CacheStore interface is public and user-implementable; a store normalising headers differently is a plausible identity differential on the protected header name.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deduplication handing one in-flight Set-Cookie response to waiters whose requests differ only in an excluded 'cookie' header
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Dedup is a neighbouring 'share one response across callers' feature; a maintainer could add a Set-Cookie bail-out there in the same spirit. Different feature, so only as a planted extra.

O9_family: CWE-524/CWE-200 information exposure via shared cache (cross-user response reuse)
